title: How do I know it's real this time?
old_caption: Real love often feels calmer than the movies. It shows up on ordinary days, and you get to feel like yourself around them. If that sounds familiar, hold on to it gently.

title: When Their Texts Get Shorter
old_caption:
Their texts went from paragraphs to "ok" and your brain wrote a whole drama.
Short texts usually mean a busy day, not a verdict on you. Ask kindly instead of guessing.

title: Missing Them, Not Going Back
old_caption:
Missing them at 2 a.m. doesn't mean you should go back.
Let the feeling visit, write it down, and text a friend instead. Missing someone is memory, not a map.

title: When You Like Them More
old_caption:
Planning every date while they just show up is a lonely kind of crush.
Say it kindly: are we on the same page? Then believe the answer they give you.

title: A Crush on Your Friend
old_caption:
A crush on your best friend feels like too much to risk.
Say it gently, give them room, and mean it when you say the friendship stays. Save this for the brave day.

title: The Night Before a First Date
old_caption:
First date tomorrow and your brain is running worst cases on a loop.
Pick the outfit tonight, bring three questions you're curious about, and remember: nerves mean you care.

title: Not Feeling It, Kindly
old_caption:
They're lovely. There's just no spark, and vanishing feels easier.
A warm, short, clear message lets them move on. Honest is kinder than a slow fade.

title: Pretending Not to Care
old_caption:
Saying "sure, whatever" when you actually mean "yes, please."
Playing it cool can hide you from the person you like. You can stay calm and still say one true thing.

title: Same Type, Same Ending
old_caption:
Same type, same ending, again?
Familiar can feel like chemistry. Write down your green flags and give the steady one a real chance.

title: The 2 a.m. "u up?" draft
old_caption:
Your thumb at 2 a.m. is not your best advisor.
Write it in your notes, put the phone face down, and decide in daylight.
